summary: The multiple-scattering sanity benchmark of geant4_benchmarks.py evaluated its Highland reference at multiple_scattering.py's defaults (100 GV, beta 1, charge 1) whatever the benchmark's particle and energy_MeV.

observables: reference_value, relative_difference and the plausibility verdict of the multiple-scattering sanity benchmark
impact.bias: the reference scales as 1 / (beta p): for a 1 GeV kinetic-energy proton (p = 1.696 GeV/c, beta = 0.875) through 0.3 mm of silicon it was 0.0147 x the correct value, so correctly distributed angles were implausible; singly charged particles near 100 GeV/c were right by coincidence (about 0.1 %)
impact.trigger: a geant4_benchmarks.py run with a multiple-scattering benchmark whose particle and energy are not a singly charged particle of about 100 GeV/c

applies_to.match_basis: a Geant4 study record (check_geant4_study.py) embeds the benchmark results of geant4_benchmarks.py in extension.study.benchmarks; a record that lists one of these benchmarks was evaluated by the affected code

outputs.how_to_recognize: geant4_benchmarks.py run output (JSON) whose benchmarks list holds benchmark multiple-scattering without highland_kinematics

remedy: rerun geant4_benchmarks.py with this version; the output now records highland_kinematics (rigidity_GV, beta, charge_number)
